children: has been granted permission to store carbon dioxide emissions in underground wells in Texas after state regulators narrowly approved its application on Tuesday, the
reported, paving the way for the company to advance a $5B-plus plan to build the world's largest carbon capture pipeline network.
The permit for the Rose carbon capture and storage project will enable Exxon
to inject ~53M metric tons of its clients' carbon emissions into three underground wells it has drilled at sites in Jefferson County, ~90 miles east of Houston.
Representatives on the Texas Railroad Commission voted two to one in favor of granting Exxon
the permit following a public hearing that reflected mounting public and political opposition to carbon capture and storage in Louisiana and Texas.
Senior VP of CCS Dominic Genetti said the decision was a "major milestone" that allows the company to continue expanding its business across the U.S. Gulf Coast.
However, analysts say the Trump administration's decision
to roll back climate rules limiting greenhouse gas emissions from power plants could dent demand for CCS technology in the power sector.

title: Texas regulator approves Exxon's $5B carbon capture project after lengthy battle
